Welcome to the clinic. I see you are an infant presenting with recurrent stridor and wheezing; could you tell me exactly when these episodes occur, such as during crying, feeding, or when lying down?

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), Heart Rate 110 bpm, Respiratory Rate 30 breaths/min. Respiratory Exam: Inspection shows mild intercostal retractions; Auscultation reveals wheezing during episodes with no crackles; Palpation and Percussion show clear lung fields and no crepitus. Cardiovascular Exam: Normal inspection, auscultation shows regular rhythm with no murmurs, palpation and percussion are normal. Neck Exam: No visible masses, swelling, or palpable tenderness. Diagnostic Imaging: Chest X-ray and Barium Swallow confirm compression of the trachea and esophagus consistent with a vascular ring; Echocardiogram confirms a double aortic arch.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Double Aortic Arch (Vascular Ring Syndrome).

The clinical findings of recurrent stridor and wheezing, combined with the definitive imaging results showing tracheal and esophageal compression by a vascular ring and confirmed on echocardiogram, establish this diagnosis.
